With compression these differ 3–10×. |\n| Sender | 1080p display, 50%+ brightness, DC-balanced frames |\n| Receiver | Mid-range Android (Pixel-6-class), rear camera |\n| Distance | 30 cm (laptop→phone), 15 cm (phone→phone) |\n| Mounting | Tripod for budget figures; handheld reported separately, never mixed |\n| Lighting | ~300 lux, no direct glare |\n| File | 1 MB of random bytes (incompressible) unless stated |\n| Duration | ≥ 60 s sustained; startup excluded |\n| Trials | ≥ 5; report median and p99, never the best run |\n\n**§15's comparison table mixes measurement regimes** — PixNet's 12 Mb/s used a 30\" LCD and\na 24 MP DSLR. Such figures MUST be labelled with their regime and never compared directly\nto handheld numbers.\n\n---\n\n## 14. Testing strategy and quality gates\n\n### 14.1 Tiers\n\n| Tier | What | Runs |\n|---|---|---|\n| **T-unit** | Codec internals, header parse, CRC, bitmap, repair-code round-trip | Every commit |\n| **T-property** | Random files × random loss patterns → byte-exact; overhead within simulation bounds | Every commit |\n| **T-stub-camera** | `getUserMedia` stubbed with `canvas.captureStream(0)` + `requestFrame()`. No flags, frame-exact, deterministic | Every commit |\n| **T-degradation** | Synthetic blur / rotation / keystone / glare / rolling-shutter tearing applied to rendered frames. **Assert decode *rates*, not booleans** | Nightly |\n| **T-real-capture** | Frames → Y4M → Chromium fake camera. Proven in research (byte-exact, including late-join at 700 ms) | Nightly |\n| **T-scale** | Synthetic 4 GB stream at the block layer; assert flat memory across 21,800 blocks | Nightly |\n| **T-long-run** | **20–30 minute sustained run** on real devices to validate thermal behavior (R11), duty-cycle economics (D27), and sustained throughput. Tracks fps decline, decode rate, and effective goodput over time. **This is the ONLY tier that can measure R11 and D27** — the 60 s floor in §13.2 structurally excludes thermal phenomena. | Weekly (or per thermal-related change) |\n| **T-physical-rig** | Two real devices, fixed mounting, the §13.2 denominator. **This is the acceptance gate for §13.1 throughput** — nothing else can measure it | Per release |\n| **T-manual-iOS** | Full pass on a real iPhone. **Not CI-testable at any price** — WebKit cannot fake a camera, the Simulator has none | Per release |\n\n> **Trap, already paid for:** `--use-fake-device-for-media-capture` **does not exist**. It\n> is `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream`, and the file flag requires it.\n\n### 14.2 Binary-safety testing\n\n**MUST use real compressed payloads at several lengths — never ASCII.** Corruption in the\nrejected libraries was both *content*- and *length*-dependent: the same generator\nround-tripped at 600 bytes and corrupted at 256. An ASCII suite marks every library safe,\nincluding the broken ones. The nastiest case, `@zxing/library.getText()`, returns the\n**correct length** while collapsing bytes ≥ 0x80 to U+FFFD — a length assertion passes and\nthe file is silently ruined. Assert on bytes, at multiple lengths, over 0x00–0xFF.\n\n### 14.3 Conformance vectors\n\nShip as fixtures, because they are what a third-party implementation would need:\n\n- `(streamId, blockIndex, seq) → index set` — bit-exact, pinning the PRNG (I3)\n- Header encode/decode round-trip at every field boundary\n- Beacon encode/decode including absent optional fields\n- Repair-code round-trip, including a deliberately mistyped code\n- A **two-realm test**: the same built app in two contexts, one sending, one receiving —\n  the only test that actually verifies the \"both roles, one page\" constraint\n\n### 14.4 The no-network assertion\n\nCI MUST fail the build if the running app issues **any** network request after load —\nincluding the lazy WASM fetch described in §6.5, which is the most likely violation and\ndoes not occur until the first decode, so **the assertion must exercise a decode**\n(intercept `fetch`/`XHR`/`WebSocket`/`EventSource`/`Image`; fail on any call). This is the\nexecutable form of T7 and of concept.md constraint 1.\n\n### 14.5 Quality gates\n\n| Gate | Requirement |\n|---|---|\n| **G1** | Typecheck, lint, unit, property, stub-camera all green |\n| **G2** | No network requests (§14.4) |\n| **G3** | Bundle-size budget not exceeded; dependencies pinned to exact versions, no post-install scripts (T5) |\n| **G4** | Simulation assertions for D5/D6/D25 pass (I2), **at the adopted K** |\n| **G5** | Memory budget (I6a) holds on T-scale. **Runs nightly**, so it gates the nightly build, not each commit — see the cadence note below |\n| **G6** | Throughput budgets (§13.1) hold on T-physical-rig — release only |\n| **G7** | `python3 docs/research/sim/ge_cost_model.py --check` passes — **the plan's §3.1/§4 numbers match what the model computes**. This exists because every critical defect found in review was a bookkeeping failure attached to correct reasoning; making the numbers executable removes the class |\n\n**All-gates-same-commit:** G1–G4 and **G7** MUST pass on the *same* commit — these are\nfast. G5 is nightly and gates the nightly build; G6 is release-only. A green build\nassembled from different commits is not a green build.\n\n### 14.6 Definition of done\n\nA phase is done when: its exit criteria (§17) are met; G1–G5 are green on one commit; every\nnew failure mode has a test; every new error code has a user-facing string; and the plan\nis updated if any decision changed.\n\n**Stop-ship criteria** — do not release if: any A-scenario fails; I1–I10 are unenforced;\na data-loss path exists without a test; or the version footer is absent (a user cannot\ntell what they are running).\n\n---\n\n## 15. Resume/Compression/T4-Reap Conflict Analysis\n\n## Problem Statement\n\n**plan.md §8.3 claims**: \"the sender is stateless across restarts by construction\" — **FALSE when compression is enabled**.\n\n### Root Cause Chain\n\n1. **Wire payload depends on compressed staging file** (D8): CompressionStream writes a compressed staging file to OPFS, then blocks are carved from it\n2. **CompressionStream offers no determinism guarantee**: Different runs, versions, or platforms may produce different compressed byte sequences for the same input\n3. **E11 reaps staging on startup**: Sender-side staging files with no active session are deleted on startup\n4. **T4 requires wiping staging for privacy**: Staging MUST be wiped on completion, cancel, and startup-reap\n5. **Sender restart → staging reaped → re-compress**: When the sender restarts, it re-compresses the source file\n6. **Different bytes → different blocks**: Re-compression produces different byte boundaries\n7. **Receiver silently corrupted**: The receiver's bitmap, block hashes, and manifest assume the old block boundaries — everything becomes invalid without detection\n\n### Why This Breaks Resume\n\n**When compression is DISABLED** (the original design):\n- Sender is stateless: Same file + same streamId = same blocks\n- streamId derived deterministically from file metadata (§7.4)\n- Receiver's bitmap stays valid across sender restarts\n\n**When compression is ENABLED**:\n- Sender's wire payload = compressed staging file\n- CompressionStream non-deterministic → re-compression produces different bytes\n- Same streamId, different block contents → receiver's bitmap points to wrong data\n- Per-block hashes (the only application-layer integrity check, §7.1) fail silently until final verification\n- Multi-GB transfer completes with corrupt output\n\n## Resolution: Forbid Resume with Compression\n\n**Decision**: Resume is NOT supported when compression is enabled.\n\n### Implementation\n\n1. **Beacon flag `RESUME_DISABLED`** (PacketFlags or beacon flags field)\n   - Sender sets this flag when `PacketFlags.Compressed` is set\n   - Receiver reads this flag from the beacon\n   - Resume UI is suppressed when this flag is present\n\n2. **Privacy constraint preserved** (T4):\n   - Staging files continue to be wiped on startup (E11)\n   - Staging files continue to be wiped on completion/cancel\n   - No change to privacy posture\n\n3. **User experience**:\n   - User selects same file → different streamId than compressed session → fresh transfer\n   - Receiver never offers resume for compressed transfers\n   - No silent corruption possible\n\n### Why This Over Alternatives\n\n**Alternative 1**: Preserve staging across restarts\n- **Rejected**: Violates T4 (privacy requirement)\n- Would require user-visible \"abandoned staging files\" clutter\n- Storage quota pressure on multi-GB files\n\n**Alternative 2**: Hash-based block boundaries\n- **Rejected**: Requires full file read to compute block boundaries\n- Defeats streaming design (D20)\n- Adds complexity for minimal benefit\n\n**Alternative 3**: Compression determinism guarantee\n- **Rejected**: CompressionStream spec offers no such guarantee\n- Would require custom WASM compressor\n- Out of scope for v1\n\n**Alternative 4**: Per-block hash mismatch detection during resume\n- **Rejected**: Requires receiver to re-verify all completed blocks on resume\n- Wastes progress (hours of transfer time)\n- Poor UX: \"resume works but throws away your work\"\n\n## Specification\n\n### Sender Behavior\n\nWhen compression is enabled:\n1. Set `PacketFlags.Compressed` on beacon packets\n2. Set `RESUME_DISABLED` flag in beacon metadata\n3. Continue normal transmission\n4. Wipe staging on completion/cancel (T4)\n5. Staging reaped on next startup (E11)\n\n### Receiver Behavior\n\nOn beacon receipt:\n1. If `RESUME_DISABLED` flag is set:\n   - Do NOT persist resume state (bitmap, metadata)\n   - Show \"Resume not available for this transfer\" message\n   - Suppress any resume UI on reload\n2. Otherwise, persist resume state normally (D22)\n\n### streamId Behavior\n\nstreamId derivation (§7.4) is UNCHANGED:\n- Same file → same streamId regardless of compression\n- This is intentional: user re-selecting file starts fresh transfer\n- Different compressed session cannot resume from/to uncompressed session\n\n## Testing\n\n### Unit Tests\n- Test that beacon sets `RESUME_DISABLED` when compression enabled\n- Test that receiver suppresses resume UI when flag present\n\n### Integration Tests\n- Compressed transfer interrupted → reload → resume UI NOT shown\n- Uncompressed transfer interrupted → reload → resume UI shown\n- Compressed then uncompressed transfer → different streamIds\n\n### Property Tests\n- For any file, compression produces deterministic blocks within ONE session\n- For any file, re-compression MAY produce different blocks across sessions\n\n## References\n\n- plan.md §8.3 (Resume D22)\n- plan.md §7.4 (streamId derivation)\n- plan.md §7.1 (Packet header and integrity)\n- plan.md §12 (Threat model T4)\n- plan.md §10 (Edge cases E11, E12)\n- plan.md D8 (Compression decision)\n- plan.md D22 (Resume requirement)\n","numLines":125,"startLine":1,"totalLines":125}}}

flag from beacon and suppresses resume UI\n   - No resume state persisted (bitmap not saved to IndexedDB)\n\n2. **StreamId behavior:**\n   - Unchanged: Same file → same streamId regardless of compression\n   - Re-selecting same file after restart → fresh transfer (not a resume)\n   - Different compressed session cannot resume from/to uncompressed session\n\n3. **User communication:**\n   - UI shows \"Resume not available with compression enabled\"\n   - Compression toggle shows trade-off: \"Speed (no resume) vs. Robustness (resume)\"\n\n#### Trade-offs\n\n| Dimension | Impact | Notes |\n|-----------|--------|-------|\n| **Privacy (T4)** | ✅ Positive | No staging persistence → T4 fully preserved |\n| **Correctness** | ✅ Positive | Explicitly disables unsafe resume → no silent corruption |\n| **Complexity** | ✅ Positive | Minimal code change (~50-100 lines) |\n| **UX** | ⚠️ Mixed | Clear trade-off: speed vs. robustness |\n| **Storage** | ✅ Positive | No staging accumulation |\n\n#### Implementation Complexity\n\n- **Low** (~50-100 lines)\n  - Add `BeaconFlags.ResumeDisabled` enum value\n  - Set flag in beacon when compression enabled\n  - Check flag in receiver resume UI rendering\n  - Update plan.md §8.3 documentation\n\n#### Risks\n\n1. **User confusion:** Users may not understand why resume is unavailable\n2. **Transfer loss:** Multi-hour transfers restart from beginning on interruption\n3. **Connection dependency:** Compression becomes viable only on stable connections\n\n---\n\n### Option C: Use Deterministic Compression\n\n**Approach:** Replace `CompressionStream` with a deterministic compressor that guarantees reproducible output.\n\n#### Mechanism\n\n1. **Custom WASM compressor:**\n   - Integrate a deterministic gzip/zlib implementation (e.g., zlib-ng)\n   - Fix compression level, strategy, and metadata\n   - Strip timestamp, filename, and other variable fields\n\n2. **Determinism guarantees:**\n   - Same input + same compressor version = identical output\n   - Cross-platform consistency via WASM\n   - Versioned compressor to detect algorithm changes\n\n3. **Fallback mechanism:**\n   - If compressor version mismatch, abort resume\n   - Beacon carries compressor version identifier\n   - Receiver validates version before persisting resume state\n\n#### Trade-offs\n\n| Dimension | Impact | Notes |\n|-----------|--------|-------|\n| **Privacy (T4)** | ✅ Positive | Staging still wiped; no persistence needed |\n| **Correctness** | ✅ Positive | Deterministic compression → safe resume |\n| **Complexity** | ❌ Negative | High complexity; custom compressor integration |\n| **UX** | ✅ Positive | Resume works with compression (best of both) |\n| **Storage** | ✅ Positive | No staging accumulation |\n\n#### Implementation Complexity\n\n- **High** (~800-1200 lines)\n  - Integrate WASM compressor build pipeline\n  - Implement compressor versioning and validation\n  - Add compressor unit tests across platforms\n  - Maintain custom WASM dependency\n  - Handle fallback when compressor unavailable\n\n#### Risks\n\n1. **Maintenance burden:** Custom WASM compressor requires ongoing updates\n2. **Build complexity:** Adds WASM compilation to build pipeline\n3. **Browser compatibility:** WASM support varies (though broadly available)\n4. **Performance:** WASM compressor may be slower than native `CompressionStream`\n5. **Version skew:** Compressor updates invalidate all existing resume states\n\n---\n\n## Trade-off Summary\n\n| Option | Privacy (T4) | Correctness | Complexity | UX | Storage | Total |\n|--------|--------------|-------------|------------|-----|---------|-------|\n| **A: Preserve staging** | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ⚠️ | ❌ | 1/5 |\n| **B: Forbid resume** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ⚠️ | ✅ | 4/5 |\n| **C: Deterministic compression** | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | 4/5 |\n\n**Key:**\n- ✅ = Positive impact (fully meets requirement)\n- ⚠️ = Mixed impact (trade-off or caveat)\n- ❌ = Negative impact (violates requirement or high cost)\n\n## Recommendation\n\n### Chosen Option: **Option B — Forbid Resume When Compression is Enabled**\n\n**Rationale:**\n\n1. **Privacy preservation (T4 compliance):** No staging persistence → privacy posture unchanged\n2. **Correctness guarantee:** Explicitly disabling unsafe resume prevents silent corruption\n3. **Low implementation complexity:** ~50-100 lines vs. 300-1200 lines for alternatives\n4. **Clear user contract:** Speed vs. robustness trade-off is transparent\n5. **No new maintenance burden:** No custom compressor or session tracking\n\n**Why not Option A (preserve staging)?**\n- Violates T4 privacy requirement (staging must be wiped)\n- Adds significant complexity (session tracking, abandonment UI)\n- Storage exhaustion risk on multi-GB files\n- Cross-platform stability issues remain (staging may not survive OS cleanup)\n\n**Why not Option C (deterministic compression)?**\n- High implementation and maintenance complexity\n- Custom WASM compressor dependency\n- Build pipeline complexity\n- Versioning issues (compressor updates invalidate resume states)\n- `CompressionStream` is fast and well-integrated — replacing it is costly\n\n**Why Option B is acceptable:**\n- Users choose between two valid modes:\n  - **Compression ON:** 3-10× faster transfers, no resume (stable connections)\n  - **Compression OFF:** Slower transfers, resume supported (unstable connections)\n- The trade-off is explicit and understandable\n- Implementation is trivial and low-risk\n- Privacy and correctness are fully preserved\n\n## Implementation Outline\n\n### Phase 1: Beacon Protocol (Priority: P0)\n\n1. **Add `ResumeDisabled` flag to beacon**\n   ```typescript\n   // src/core/frame/beacon.ts\n beacon construction\n   if (compressionEnabled) {\n     flags |= BeaconFlags.Compressed | BeaconFlags.ResumeDisabled;\n   }\n   ```\n\n3. **Update plan.md §8.3** to document restriction explicitly\n\n### Phase 2: Receiver Resume Logic (Priority: P0)\n\n1. **Check flag before persisting resume state**\n   ```typescript\n   // Receiver beacon handler\n   if ((beacon.flags & BeaconFlags.ResumeDisabled) !== 0) {\n     // Do NOT persist bitmap or metadata\n     showResumeDisabledMessage();\n     return;\n   }\n   ```\n\n2. **Suppress resume UI when flag present**\n   ```typescript\n   // UI rendering\n   const canResume = !isResumeDisabled(beacon.flags) && hasPersistedState();\n   ```\n\n### Phase 3: User Communication (Priority: P1)\n\n1. **Add clear messaging:**\n   - \"Resume is not available when compression is enabled\"\n   - \"To enable resume, disable compression in settings\"\n\n2. **Compression toggle tooltip:**\n   - \"Compression: Faster tests:**\n   - Test beacon flag setting when compression enabled\n   - Test receiver resume suppression when flag present\n\n2. **Integration tests:**\n   - Compressed transfer interrupted → reload → resume UI NOT shown\n   - Uncompressed transfer interrupted → reload → resume UI shown\n   - Beacon flag validation end-to-end\n\n3. **Property tests:**\n   - For any file, compression produces deterministic blocks within ONE session\n   - For any file, re-compression MAY produce different blocks across sessions\n\n### Phase 5: Documentation (Priority: P1)\n\n1. **Update plan.md:**\n   -
